messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Elevated 5xx spike detected for private-gw-eu-1 -> increase in gateway 5xx/timeouts since 2026-03-15T10:12Z. Auto-paging: @SRE Oncall
Ellie: ack. paging @SRE Oncall and @ops-bot. seeing customer errors too. starting triage.
SRE Oncall: on it, taking lead. status: investigating NAT/egress for private clusters in eu-west.
Sam: graph: p95 latency up, 5xx rate 6.8% across private routes. Hosted endpoints unaffected. Only customers using private VPC egress via private-gw-eu-1.
Jules: I can run quick checks on NAT GW metrics + conntrack. give me a minute.
Tran: I deployed a quick metric alert dashboard for ephemeral port usage last week. jumping in.
Jules: aws cloudwatch shows NATGatewayBytes/ActiveConnections normal but NAT Gateway Port utilization (custom) > 92% on private-gw-eu-1. conntrack entries spiking. suspect ephemeral port exhaustion.
Sam: logs from gateway show repeated: "upstream read timeout" and "504 Gateway Time-out". example curl output from an affected path:
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Host: customer-a'
* Connected to 10.0.5.17:443
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: customer-a
< HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Time-out
< Server: redwood-gateway
```
Jules: running `sudo conntrack -S` shows ephemeral slot exhaustion on nodes in private-gw-eu-1. ``conntrack table: 65536 entries`` and `inuse = 64000`.
Ellie: any recent SG/ACL changes? Could this be a security group limiting ephemeral ports?
Tran: checked audit logs — no SG changes in last 12h. I did see a targeted rollout earlier this morning that changed an egress proxy config for a single customer — rolling back now to test.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback triggered by @Tran on service: egress-proxy-config (rev: canary-2026-03-15-09:40)
Sam: rolling back didn't reduce 5xx immediately. still high.
Jules: tcpdump snippet on gateway node (filtered):
```
13:46:02.123456 IP 10.0.5.22.54832 > 198.51.100.23.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
13:46:02.123789 IP 10.0.5.22.54833 > 198.51.100.23.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
... many SYNs, few SYN-ACKs. lots of retries -> suggests upstream drop or ephemeral exhaustion locally.
```
Ellie: can we confirm NAT mapping table size? are we using a single NAT-GW per az?
Jules: yes, private-gw-eu-1 backs two AZs but a single NAT gateway per AZ configured. Port range tight because of early OS defaults. current kernel conntrack max = 65536. we should increase to 262144 and tune tcp_tw_reuse.
SRE Oncall: immediate mitigations: 1) increase conntrack max on gateway pool, 2) temporarily add second NAT gateway in same AZ to increase port space, 3) enable fallback egress route for affected customers to use public egress path. I'll coordinate.
Tran: running bootstrap to bump conntrack: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` on affected nodes now.
Jules: applied. conntrack slots increased. monitoring graph shows drop from 99% -> 64% usage over next 30s.
Sam: 5xx rate reduced from 6.8% -> 2.1% after conntrack bump. still above baseline (0.1%).
Ellie: proceed with adding second NAT GW. @ops-bot can you create nat-gw-eu-1b in az-a and attach to the private route table for the affected subnet?
ops-bot: infra-bot: creating NAT Gateway nat-gw-eu-1b in eu-west-1a. updating route table rtb-0a1b2c -> target nat-gw-eu-1b.
ops-bot: infra-bot: NAT gateway available. routes updated. health checks green.
Sam: monitoring shows further drop: 5xx -> 0.6%. majority of affected customers now stable.
Jules: still seeing a handful of timeouts consistent with a single upstream peer refusing connections — investigating peering path to Partner-P transit.
Ellie: any firewall / partner filters? Could peering asymmetry cause half-open handshakes?
Tran: checked peering route tables — one propagated route to partner prefix was missing on the eu-west router for subnet 10.0.5.0/24. adding the route now.
Tran: route propagated. peering session flaps in last hour correlate with route propagation window during a control-plane update.
Sam: with NAT ports expanded and second NAT GW, service errors are now under 0.2% and trending normal.
Ellie: Customer impact summary for status page: ~7 customers on Private VPC with heavy egress saw intermittent 504/5xx between 10:12Z and 10:48Z. Peak error rate ~6.8%. Mitigations applied: conntrack increased, additional NAT gateway provisioned, peering route repaired. No data loss; requests may have been retried by clients.
Jules: Action items (immediate): 1) add persistent kernel tuning to image (conntrack_max=262144 + tcp_tw_reuse), 2) add alert for conntrack utilization > 80% per gateway, 3) add automation to spin up secondary NAT when utilization > 70%.
SRE Oncall: Handoff: I'm passing to @Jules for follow-ups and postmortem. Next on-call please track customer triage and status page updates.
Jules: taking handoff. brief summary: root cause = ephemeral port exhaustion exacerbated by transient peering route propagation; mitigations = conntrack increase + extra NAT + route fix + rollback unaffected. timeframe: 10:12Z - 10:48Z.
Ellie: sending customer-subscriber notice and paging CS to prepare targeted comms.
ops-bot: statuspage: incident created (INC-2026-0315-01) - Investigating -> Update posted.
Tran: I'll own the follow-up for runbook updates and automation for NAT scaling. filing GH issue and tagging infra team.
Sam: quick note for postmortem: check NAT endpoint pooling for private clusters, ensure we don't rely on single nat-gw per busy subnet, audit control-plane release timing during peering route propagation windows.
Jules: thanks team. marking thread resolved for paging. will update when postmortem is drafted. :white_check_mark:
